candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — antineoplastic pharmacology
candidate.educational_objective: Identify methotrexate as a folate analog metabolic inhibitor whose antineoplastic action includes inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase and interference with purine, thymidylate, and DNA synthesis.

options.A: Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase, reducing tetrahydrofolate-dependent purine and thymidylate synthesis and interfering with DNA synthesis and replication.
options.B: Induction of DNA strand breaks through interaction with DNA topoisomerase II, producing cell-cycle arrest and cell death.
options.C: Formation of interstrand and intrastrand DNA cross-links that interfere with normal transcription and DNA replication.
options.D: Stabilization of microtubules by preventing depolymerization, disrupting the dynamic microtubule changes required for mitosis.

candidate.rationale: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, preventing normal tetrahydrofolate-dependent synthesis of purine nucleotides and thymidylate and thereby interfering with DNA synthesis, repair, and cellular replication. A is therefore correct. B describes the topoisomerase-II-associated DNA strand-break mechanism of etoposide, C describes cisplatin DNA cross-linking, and D describes paclitaxel-mediated microtubule stabilization. These are plausible antineoplastic mechanisms but are not methotrexate's mechanism.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolic acid reductase; reduced tetrahydrofolates are required for purine nucleotide and thymidylate synthesis, so methotrexate interferes with DNA synthesis, repair, and cellular replication.
